text: Case Number: SF-2026-685423  Pursuant to Sri Lanka's *Motor Traffic Act*, we hereby officially notify you that a vehicle registered in your name has been identified as having violated road traffic regulations. This violation was automatically detected and recorded by a fixed traffic surveillance system (Device Code: VRM-865).  To view details regarding the violation and to pay the associated fine, please visit the following link: [**https://govpay.cfd/en/spot-fine**](https://govpay.cfd/en/spot-fine)  In accordance with current road traffic regulations, please ensure that the fine is settled within 14 days.

reply.reason: This is a classic fake government-fine lure: it claims a traffic camera ("Device Code: VRM-865") caught a vehicle registered in your name and pushes you to pay within 14 days, using a deadline to rush you before you check anything. The payment link, https://govpay.cfd/en/spot-fine, does not belong to any Sri Lankan government domain (official services use .gov.lk), and the .cfd address space is commonly used for throwaway scam pages; the local scanner also flagged it for a hostile link shape, supporting a hostile-destination reading rather than a real payment portal. The message is generic — no vehicle plate, no verifiable case reference — and it asks you to click a link and pay rather than directing you to an official portal or confirming details through a known channel. I could not verify the link, so it should be treated as unverified and unsafe; do not open or pay through it, and check directly with the relevant Sri Lankan authority using a number or site you find yourself.
